возиться.gloss: to fiddle with, potter about, bustle

meanings.en: to potter about, fiddle, fuss over

examples.trans: Stop fussing around in the kitchen!
The children pottered with the construction set for a long time.

examples.text: Нина, хорош там возиться на кухне!
examples.trans: Nina, stop fussing around in the kitchen!

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.trans: As you all know...
Does the governor support you?

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

выходить.gloss: to go out, to get out

meanings.en: to go out, to come out
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go out, to get out', paired with 'выйти'.

examples.trans: I'm going out in a minute.
Come out!

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
examples.trans: You give me five hundred roubles, and I get out and buy you the best console in the world.
Let's talk.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: plural only: there is no singular in everyday use

examples.trans: I have no money.

подъехать.gloss: to drive up, arrive by car

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ъехать'). Used as an verbal verb meaning 'to drive up, arrive by car'.

examples.trans: I can drive over there too!

examples.text: Такси уже подъехало к нашему дому.
examples.trans: The taxi has already driven up to our house.

meanings.en: to be quiet, to keep silent for a bit
meanings.note: politer or softer than молчать in commands

examples.trans: Please be quiet.

examples.text: Помолчите, пожалуйста. Не видите, человеку плохо?

присесть.gloss: to sit down (for a moment), to take a seat

meanings.en: to sit down, to have a seat

examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, have a seat.

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, присядьте. Попробуйте чай с сушками, очень вкусные.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, have a seat. Try the tea with bread rings, they're very tasty.

meanings.en: to check, to test, to verify
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'верить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to check, to test', paired with 'проверять'.

examples.trans: Check the soldering iron.
We'll check everything right now.

examples.text: Вот с таким настроением и иди к Аникееву. Паяльник проверь.

examples.text: Тогда прощай, я должен срочно уйти.
examples.trans: Then farewell, I must urgently leave.
Farewell, our old communal apartment!

meanings.note: comparative of скоро used as adverb or particle

examples.trans: Let's go quickly to the studio!
Rather yes than no.
Bring the clothespin quickly!

скучать.gloss: to miss, yearn for, feel bored

examples.text: Я буду очень скучать по вам.
examples.trans: I will miss you very much.

examples.trans: Quite right, I am the mayor of this town. And my offer to you is this.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'оседка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'neighbor (female)' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The neighbor told everything.

examples.text: Соседка нам уже всё давно рассказала.
examples.trans: The neighbor already told us everything long ago.

examples.text: Спасибо вам за всё, соседка дорогая.
examples.trans: Thank you for everything, dear neighbor.

meanings.note: спасибо за + accusative = thank you for

examples.trans: Thanks, Dad!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good, nice').

хотя.gloss: even if, at least (with бы); although
